claim: The running system is already a two-model chain: tier 1 routes and never replies, tier 2 answers, the two share only a free-text note, and a tier-2 timeout discards tier 1. Neither prompt holds a customer fact.
note: Both refuters confirmed every cited line.

claim: The model has no read path to the ledger and the home card's Transactions line has no handler.
note: Overstated as written. The model can trigger two point lookups it never sees the result of (balance; latest deposit or pay-out status, pay-outs added on 16 September). There is no transaction list, statement or history read. The conclusion (build the pack first) holds.

claim: History is lopsided and duplicated: 3 customer-side writes against 59 bot-side, the current message written before the 5-line read so it appears twice, and a non-atomic rewrite of the whole JSON column on every write.
note: Counts verified by repo-wide grep; fast copy byte-identical to the iCloud repo.

claim: The withdrawal truth is split per customer: home, the withdraw matcher and how-it-works use the per-customer pilot list, while the AI's knowledge and prompt read the global switch.
note: Verified at every cited line; the pilot-gate test greps only for the global function, so it passes.

claim: Three execute routes are public and mis-ordered (no internal auth, PIN verified before preview ownership, no crash release), and only 2 of the PIN states are strict.
note: Verified; the middleware never touches /api, and the capabilities doc overstates what the code enforces.

claim: Delivery is at-most-once with silent loss: the message is claimed before processing, never released, and every error is acknowledged as success.
note: Verified; no release, no status column, no replay job exists.

claim: About 28 test files read the processor as text; relocating or exporting flow starters fails a large share of the suite.
note: 27 files read it as text. Relocating breaks them; exporting in place breaks nothing (locks match by substring). So flow starters are exported where they are, not injected or moved.

claim: The one-round-trip pack is not new ground: raw SQL is already used in 13 places and a seven-query customer pack already exists in the admin CRM.
note: Verified; the only test guards are against the unsafe raw-SQL variant.

claim: Removing tier 1 and the every-turn how-it-works block cuts prompt volume by at least a third, and a reply-only turn lands under 3 seconds at p50.
note: Both refuters trimmed it. Measured from the delivered prompts: roughly a third less on today's two-call turns, and a net increase on the single-call fast-path turns (about a third of the corpus); the real saving is the uncached tier-1 call and the context sent twice. The latency figure was an unlogged impression, not a measurement; every latency on this page is a target for the eval runner.

claim: WhatsApp cannot stream or edit a sent message; the repo sends no typing indicator; Meta's messages endpoint accepts a read status with a typing indicator that shows for up to 25 seconds.
note: Verified against the repo and Meta's typing-indicators page, fetched 16 September 2026.

claim: Every rand still moves only through the existing preview, confirm, PIN and execute contract, and every PIN state requires a preview id so no proposal can enter at the PIN step.
note: The safety conclusion holds, two mechanisms were wrong: the pay-out and pay-request PIN states are gated by flow-owned state, not a preview id, and the dispatcher has no withdraw action today. Restated: the dispatcher may only start a flow at its first step, never sets a confirm or PIN state, never imports a ledger writer; a dead non-idempotent wallet writer in the domain package is to be deleted.

claim: A customer-events read model keyed by ledger idemKey, backfilled nightly and sum-checked against the journal, converges to the ledger within a day.
note: An idemKey is per journal entry, not per customer (one send touches two wallets), and holds, pending and failed pay-outs never reach the journal at all, so that table could not show the founder's parked PayShap. The pack now reads the source tables directly in one batch, as the admin CRM does; per-account journal columns come later.
